description:
State on develop 7faa29377 (stream flattening fz-sc8.150 and evidence-row fold fz-sc8.151 merged). The distiller's compile stops at the 50,000-request product budget after ~2 s; with the budget raised it settles at 63,457 requests in 3.2 s and then fails at fz-sc8.3 (:erlang.float_to_binary). This ticket closes when the compile finishes inside the default budget.

Anatomy of the settled root session (scratch an146/ in the fz-xxd13-build session; scripts ext.py census.py act.py axes.py cnt.py; trace dist.jsonl):
- 63,457 requests, 40,784 distinct product keys (1.56 requests per key; 22,673 are repeats, led by reach 'all' keys at ~64 each), 13,241 jobs, 1,738 activations over 510 functions, 1,612 executables. transport_shape is 37,847 requests / 29,147 keys, ~18 keys per executable.
- It is not a whole-program cross product. Scale: main returning 1 = 340 requests; one Enum.reduce over a list literal = 659; one Enum.reduce over an any value = 8,487 (290 activations); each further any-typed reduce site of the same shape adds ~565 requests and ~17 activations, linearly.
- Activations pile up in the functions that take a reducer closure and an accumulator: Enum.reduce/3#lambda@0/2 181 (26 reducers, ~7 each), Stream.compose/2#lambda@0/2 121, List.reduce/3 52.

One verified multiplier (cross-site mixing inside a group):
- Reduce sites over an any receiver that start from the same initial accumulator type share ONE Enumerable.Stream.reduce/3 activation: its key is (%Stream{enum: any, funs: list}, {:cont, <initial acc>}, a2) with the reducer a type variable. Each site's reducer is then analysed with every sibling site's accumulator types.
- 7-line repro an146/gen/two.fz: two reduces from [], one consing e, one consing {e, 6}. Site a's lambda gets 12 activations including (any, list({any, int})), a type only site b builds. Output is right on interp; only work is wasted.
- Controlled series, 8 sites: same initial accumulator = 30,364 requests, 224 reduce-lambda and 162 compose-lambda activations, 2 Stream.reduce activations; distinct initial accumulators = 23,825 requests, 62 and 50, 9.
- In the distiller four sites (subject, main, timeline, wakes) start from [] and share one activation; the top 6 reducers hold 127 of the 181 reduce-lambda activations.
- Where it is broadcast (read from the trace, mechanism inferred): DeriveRuntimeDemand on the shared Enumerable.Stream.reduce/3 activation writes RuntimeDemandInput for every Stream.compose/2 instantiation; call_return_demand_contributions (jobs/runtime_demand.rs ~997-1030) pushes the same delivered demand to every local target of a callsite.

Ruled out as the cause of the 63,457 (each fixed or spiked, none moved it): stream-in-stream nesting (fz-sc8.150), evidence rows not folding (fz-sc8.151), a caller reading the callee's joined callable-parameter demand (OptionParser's fz-sc8.127 spike, k127c/k127d).

Other measured components, no counterfactual yet: repeated requests (36%); 126 activations analysed but never made executable; 108 activation_inputs.budget_collapsed events; the fixed ~8,000-request cost of the first any-typed reduce (every Enumerable implementation is reached).

Open question to settle with a spike before any design: how far below 63,457 the distiller lands when the shared-accumulator mixing is removed (the 8-site series suggests about a fifth fewer requests, which is close to the budget line, so the mixing alone may not be enough).

comments.text: 2026-11-13, base f04c56f8e (stack rebased onto develop e1e941f42). With the Stream flattening scratch change (fz-sc8.127 step 1) the distiller's 'did not settle waiting on transport_shape' is the 50,000-request product budget, not a stuck fact: the root session needs 63,457 requests (30,838 distinct product keys, steady ~3,300 new per 5,000 requests, no loop, max repeat 65). 514 functions; most activations: Enum.reduce/3#lambda@0/2 (354) and Stream.compose/2#lambda@0/2 (144), differing in captured reducer and accumulator/entry types; Enumerable.Stream.reduce/3 is activated with %Stream{enum: any, funs: list} from any-typed Enum.reduce sites. So the residue of this ticket after step 1 is ~27% over budget, from the any receiver reaching the Stream impl at every any-typed reduce. With the budget raised the compile finishes in 2.6 s and the next divergences appear: (a) Kernel.to_string/1 'missed an exhaustive dispatch' on a 132-line cut (also on head without the scratch change: sts2/w2.exs); (b) full distiller: 'function 93 (Distill.fmt_ms/1) entry 1 step evaluation failed: StructField: subject is not a map or Struct'. Without the scratch change, head still exhausts the fact-wait budget (62 s). Evidence: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz-xxd13-build/d6960461-b7a2-4585-a9e7-9f2477e57ee2/scratchpad/sts2.

2026-11-13 evening, develop 7faa29377 (.150 stream flattening and .151 evidence-row fold merged): OptionParser traced and spiked the remaining fz-sc8.127 defect (a caller reads the callee's whole joined callable-parameter demand; k127c/k127d reports) and it does NOT move the distiller: still 63,457 requests on base and spike. So the residue here is not .127. A fresh anatomy is running (scratch an146/): census by product kind, activations per function against call sites, cross product vs per-site growth on an N-site series.

Reproduced on develop ac3750d1e + #454/#453: the cross-site pairing is also a correctness hole, not only wasted work. OptionParser's 13-line typed repro (scratch grok/err.fz in its session): two Enum.reduce over [1,2,3] seeded [], one lambda does h + e on the accumulator head, the other conses {e, 6}. Elixir prints {[6, 3, 1], [{3, 6}, {2, 6}, {1, 6}]}; fz2 interp rejects with spec/violation +/2 ({int, int}, int) at the first lambda. Either site alone compiles. No any, no streams. OptionParser is writing the re-proposal for the user; a measuring spike (scratch sp146/) is running for the any/Stream variant.

Measuring spike (scratch sp146/, patches counterfactual_keying.patch, trace.patch; nothing landed). Mechanism confirmed by trace: the sharing is in activation keys, not at the broadcast. call_return_demand_contributions (runtime_demand.rs ~1029) faithfully sends one shared activation's joined surfaces to every target; the activations are shared because (1) tail_value_uses for a ClosureCall asks nothing of the callee value, so a recursive body (List.reduce_cont/3) collapses the reducer to a free variable, and (2) derive_activation_key_arrow / erase_closure_identity erase closure brands in non-consuming forwarders (Enumerable.List/Map/Range.reduce/3). Counterfactual keeping closure identity in both places (the forwarder half is a '.reduce' label probe, not a design): two.fz site-a lambda 12 -> 5 activations, all its own; sharedL_8 becomes identical to splitL_8 (224/162 -> 46/42 lambda activations, 30,364 -> 27,046 requests); splitL_8 rises 23,825 -> 27,090; distiller activations fall (181 -> 100, 121 -> 51) and wall 2.96 s -> 1.69 s but requests RISE 63,457 -> 68,746 (distinct keys 40,784 -> 46,458). fixture_matrix: 3118 passed, 1 failed (many_senders_into_one_guarded_receive...: interp park count 0 -> 48, reproducible, undiagnosed). Conclusion: de-mixing by forking forwarder keys does not bring the distiller under 50,000; the request count is dominated by per-key product cost, not by the mixed activations. Not tried: per-target narrowing at the broadcast; the principled forwarding-edge form; whether the counterfactual fixes the typed err.fz rejection.

Probe: with sp146/counterfactual_keying.patch applied, fz2 interp on OptionParser's typed err.fz prints {[6, 3, 1], [{3, 6}, {2, 6}, {1, 6}]} (Elixir's output) instead of the spec/violation. So keeping closure identity in the keys fixes the wrong rejection; it does not fix the request budget.

Request anatomy on baseline B = develop + OptionParser's fz-sc8.127 spike (scratch ts146/; measuring only). A = 63,457 requests / 40,784 keys; B = 53,684 / 34,327. A request is one ProductDriver::pull (pull.rs ~2641); a waiting key costs two pulls (discover, resume) and memo hits count. Findings on A: (1) transport_shape 29,147 keys sit on 11,118 (function, local position) pairs and only 426 distinct answers; in 10,270 pairs every executable gives the same answer (9,045 redundant keys). Enum.reduce/3#lambda (177 executables) and Stream.compose/2#lambda (119) hold 15% of transport keys. (2) 5,739 of 6,855 waiting transport keys wait on exactly one child and 5,097 return that child's answer (alias hops); predicted ~10k requests if read through, unmeasured. (3) Repeats: transport 8,700 = its waiting evaluations exactly; wait lists are single-element because evaluate_transport_recipe returns the first Waiting (jobs/transport.rs ~1062, ~1083). Re-runs never re-request a current product. (4) One recursive group of 102 reach keys takes 3,391 requests (~64 each for 76 keys) against ~204 ideal; 17,789 of 22,373 listed waits repeat the previous round; predicted ~-3,190, unmeasured. (5) Fixed cost: JSON decode alone is 6,248 requests; one any-typed reduce adds 2,242. Counterfactual C (transport recipes return all waiting children, ~25 lines in jobs/transport.rs, patch ts146/cfT_transport_rs.patch): B 53,684 -> 52,352, keys and jobs unchanged, outputs identical, fixture_matrix 3119 passed 0 failed. Still 2,352 over. Prediction: C + the reach group fix lands near 49,100.

Reach-group spike (scratch rg146/, measuring only). On C (= .127 spike + transport multi-wait, 52,352): a 14-line change in pull.rs (E5_pull_commit_no_pending_cascade.patch) brings the distiller to 48,825 requests, so its compile FINISHES on the default 50,000 budget; keys 34,327 and jobs 11,604 unchanged. Mechanism: reach groups are already computed once and shared (stage_recursive_group); the waste is that every product commit invalidates its pending readers AND cascades to their pending readers (mutate_product_wave, pull.rs ~1289-1304), erasing the pending formulas the cycle search (pending_strong_component) needs, so the group is re-swept after each small settle: the 102-member group takes 3,391 requests (101 first evals, 494 changed-wait re-evals, 1,103 identical-wait re-evals, 1,692 cache hits). E5: an invalidation seeded by commit_members does not cascade past the first pending reader; fact-seeded and explicit invalidations keep the cascade (dropping it everywhere, E4, breaks 3 reach/retained-recursion tests). Results: 102-group 3,391 -> 431; reach:all 4,945 -> 1,879; two.fz/sharedL_8/splitL_8 outputs byte-identical; fixture_matrix 3119/0; lib: one new failure, pull_test::changed_group_drains_produced_and_pending_reader_diamond_in_semantic_order, which pins the cascade. Also measured: E1 (skip re-pull of an already-current owner) alone gives 50,043; E1+E5 unmeasured (predicted ~-543 more). Unsound and rejected: E2, E3, E4. After the compile finishes the distiller fails at run time in Distill.fmt_ms/1: 'StructField: subject is not a map or Struct'. Not verified: E5's soundness beyond the suites; run/build paths; lib on C alone shows 4 failures (3 are the .127 spike's known ones; the 4th needs attributing).

Gate on the combined stack (fz-sc8.127 7764bbe51 + fz-sc8.155 aa4886c9e + fz-sc8.156 8b3c07eca, scratch gate/fz2_all, DEFAULT budget): the distiller's compile finishes on interp, run and build. 50,249 requests summed over all sessions. All three paths then fail at run time at Distill.fmt_ms/1 (:erlang.float_to_binary): interp 'StructField: subject is not a map or Struct'; run and the built binary panic 'fz_map_get scalar key: ExpectedTag'. That is fz-sc8.3. PRs: #469 (.127), #473 (.155, stacked on #469), #474 (.156, on develop). This ticket closes when all three are merged and the distiller compile is re-measured on develop.

title: The distiller's compile finishes
